title: Father wants second inquiry into police shooting
article: The father of a man who was shot and killed by police two years ago is not satisfied with the fatality inquiry that wrapped up Wednesday.
Daniel Lippa, 29,was shot seven times outside his north-side apartment building in March 2005 after his estranged wife called 911 to say Lippa hadthreatened to kill her and her child.
During the inquiry, several police officers testified that Lippa refused to drop his knife and advanced on officers who told him to stop.
However, Cyndi Pashko told theinquiry she watched the incident from her second-storey bedroom window anddidn't seeLippacarrying a knifeor aggressively approaching the officers.
Lippa's father Ernie said there are too many discrepancies in the witness statements.
"Something is just not right, something smells," he said.
Lippa said he has asked Alberta's solicitor general for another inquiry into the shooting - this time by the new independent police oversight board being set up to review complaints against police.
"Police should never be allowed to investigate themselves. There is too much opportunity for misinformation and lies," he said.
The final report from the fatality inquiry is expected to be ready in about two months.
